messages.content: Pack my bag for a day at the zoo: list exactly four items, numbered, with each item three words or fewer.

1. Water bottle
2. Sun hat
3. Small snack box
4. Comfortable walking shoes
Describe a sleepy panda in one sentence of fewer than 15 words.
A sleepy panda curls up beside the bamboo and begins to snore.
Write three quiz questions about the water cycle, one per line, with no numbers. Question form only.

What do we call water turning into vapour?
What falls from clouds when the drops grow heavy?
Where does most rain end up in the end?
Give me a Pongal greeting in all lowercase letters, exactly two lines.

happy pongal to you and your family!
may your home be full of warmth and good rice.
List five spices from an Indian kitchen, one per line, in alphabetical order.

cardamom
cinnamon
cloves
cumin
turmeric
Could you write a haiku about waiting for a friend?

The clock ticks slowly
I watch the door for my friend
Then I hear her step
Before a run I want three warm-up moves. Give them as bullet points that start with a plus sign.

+ Gentle ankle circles
+ Slow leg swings
+ Easy marching on the spot
Describe a foggy morning in exactly nine words.
Fog covers the road, and everything sounds very quiet.
I need a note for the bathroom mirror. Under 12 words, and it must begin with the word Please.
Please close the tap tightly after you wash.
Text my friend Rohan that I will be ten minutes late. One sentence, and include the word "sorry".
Sorry, Rohan, I will be about ten minutes late.
Name four trees you might find in an Indian village. Comma-separated, all lowercase, nothing else.
neem, banyan, mango, peepal
Give me three English words that start with "sh", numbered, and nothing else.

1. shine
2. shelf
3. shoulder
One-line blurb for a mystery novel about a missing violin, please. Use the word "whisper" and stay under 20 words.
A violin vanishes from a silent hall, and only a whisper can lead the detective to it.
How do I cross a busy road safely? Four numbered steps, each six words or fewer.

1. Stop at the kerb.
2. Look right, then left.
3. Wait until the traffic is clear.
4. Walk straight across.
Two sentences about the sitar, with the first one a question.
Have you ever heard the sitar's rich, buzzing sound? It has a long neck and many strings that ring together.
Using the word "and", write a sentence about a stationery shop that lists three things I can buy there.
At the stationery shop I can buy pencils, notebooks and erasers.
Explain gravity to a child in exactly two sentences, and keep the word "force" out of it.
Gravity is what pulls things down toward the ground. It is why a dropped ball falls instead of floating away.
A four-line poem about grandmothers, please, in which every line starts with the letter G.

Gentle hands that braid my hair,
Golden stories by the stair,
Grains of love in every meal,
Grandma's hugs are warm and real.
Name six places you would find in a small town, one per line, sorted from A to Z.

bakery
bank
library
market
post office
temple
My out-of-office reply needs exactly three sentences and the word "return". Can you write it?
Thank you for your email. I am away from the office this week. I will reply as soon as I return.
I am learning to draw. Give two tips for a beginner, as a numbered list with no more than eight words per tip.

1. Practise drawing simple shapes every day.
2. Look closely at what you are drawing.
Describe a late evening in exactly eight words, all in capital letters.
STREET LIGHTS FLICKER AS THE CITY SLOWLY SLEEPS
In one sentence, say what a keyboard is. Do not use the words "type" or "typing".
A keyboard is a set of keys you press to put letters and numbers into a computer.
Suggest three things to wear on a rainy day. Bullet points with an asterisk, and no more than two words each.

* Raincoat
* Rubber boots
* Waterproof cap
Write a sentence about marigolds that uses both "orange" and "sunlight".
The orange marigolds glowed in the morning sunlight.
Write a classroom rule that begins with "Always" and ends with the word "quietly".
Always push your chair in and leave the room quietly.
Describe the taste of a spicy samosa in exactly 10 words.
A crisp shell holds spicy potatoes that tingle your tongue.
I need a cheer for our school relay team. It should rhyme and be under 10 words.
Run, run, run, we have just begun!
Name three animals that live in forests, one per line, in reverse alphabetical order.

tiger
owl
deer
Write a postcard line from Shimla in a single sentence of exactly eleven words.
The pine trees are tall and the air feels wonderfully fresh.
A friend of mine feels shy at parties. Comfort her in two sentences without using the word "brave".
Feeling shy is completely normal, and many people feel the same way. Take your time, and I will be right beside you.
Eid wish, please: under 15 words, and it should include the word "peace".
Eid Mubarak! May your day be filled with peace and joy.
Name three objects a magnet attracts. Numbered, one word each.

1. Nail
2. Paperclip
3. Needle
Write a seven-word sentence in which no two words start with the same letter.
My little sister always eats fresh grapes.
Say thank you to my father for teaching me to ride a bicycle. One sentence, and end it with an exclamation mark.
Thank you, Papa, for holding the seat until I could ride on my own!
A haiku about a river at dawn, please.

Mist lifts from the stream
Pale light spills across the stones
The river wakes up
Give me a checklist for starting a meeting on time. Use exactly the labels "Step 1:", "Step 2:" and "Step 3:" at the start of the lines.

Step 1: Open the room early.
Step 2: Share the agenda.
Step 3: Begin at the planned time.
Describe a busy traffic signal in one sentence, without the words "car" or "cars".
Buses, bikes and autos wait together while the red light glows overhead.
Make up a title for an adventure book. Exactly four words, every word capitalised.
The Lost Mountain Map
Give three reminders for keeping a desk tidy, numbered, each under eight words.

1. Put pens back in the box.
2. Stack your books neatly.
3. Throw away old paper.
Compose one sentence on stamp collecting that includes the word "rare" and has fewer than 18 words.
My grandfather keeps a small box of stamps, and one of them is very rare.
A lullaby line for a baby, please, with exactly six words.
Sleep, little one, the moon watches.
At a railway station, which four things can you see? Give them separated by commas, in alphabetical order.
bench, platform, signboard, ticket counter
Write two sentences about a summer storm, and make the second one a question.
Dark clouds rolled over the hills in minutes. Did you hear the thunder?
Describe a crow with exactly three adjectives, separated by commas and nothing else.
clever, noisy, black
Make a sleepover invitation as an acrostic of FUN, one line for each letter.

Friends, come over for a sleepover this Saturday.
Unroll your sleeping bags in my living room.
Night games and popcorn are waiting!
What is a noun? Answer in one sentence under 15 words that includes the word "thing".
A noun is a word that names a person, place or thing.
List three things people do at a wedding celebration. Bullet points that start with the symbol ">".

> Dance to lively music
> Share a big meal
> Bless the couple
Give me one sentence about the ocean that starts with "Under" and ends with "light".
Under the waves, fish glide through shafts of light.
How do I make toast? Exactly three numbered steps, each under nine words.

1. Put a slice of bread in the toaster.
2. Wait until it turns golden brown.
3. Take it out and add butter.
Which four verbs describe what you do in a science lab? Comma-separated, in alphabetical order.
measure, mix, observe, pour
Write me a haiku on a monkey sitting on a roof.

A monkey sits still
Watching the street from the roof
Then it takes my fruit
Write a Raksha Bandhan message from a brother to his sister. Exactly two sentences, with the word "promise".
Happy Raksha Bandhan, Didi! I promise to always stand by you.
Explain how to cut a mango in four numbered steps. Keep each step under eight words.

1. Wash the mango well.
2. Stand it on a board.
3. Slice off each side.
4. Scoop out the flesh with a spoon.
Describe the wind in one sentence where no word is longer than five letters.
The wind blew hard and shook the old tree.
Give me a pre-journey check for a long train trip: three dash bullets, each under six words.

- Your ticket and ID
- Phone charger
- Water for the trip
How can I ask a shopkeeper if he has a blue notebook? Give me one polite question, under 12 words.
Excuse me, do you have a blue notebook, please?
What does a printer do? Reply in under 15 words and avoid the word "paper".
A printer turns words and pictures on a screen into something you can hold.
Come up with a cheerful slogan for a school health week poster. Exactly five words.
Eat well, play hard, smile!
Write a bedtime wish from a mother to her child on two lines. The second line must begin with "Tomorrow".

Sleep well, my little star.
Tomorrow we will fly your new kite.
Ask a classmate for her science notes in a single polite sentence that includes the word "borrow".
Could I borrow your science notes for tonight, please?
Define a flyover in under ten words.
A concrete bridge that lifts traffic above the junction.
Which four things can you find on a beach? Lowercase, comma-separated, and in alphabetical order.
crab, sand, shell, wave
You are a cricket commentator. Describe a six in exactly two sentences, using the word "boundary".
The batter swings hard and the ball sails high. It clears the boundary rope and the crowd roars.
Review an imaginary children's book in three lines labelled "Plot:", "Characters:" and "Verdict:".

Plot: A girl finds a map in her school library.
Characters: Mina is curious, and her friend Dev is funny.
Verdict: A quick, cheerful read.
Give the plurals of box, child, leaf and mouse, in that order, on one line separated by commas.
boxes, children, leaves, mice
List three percussion instruments in reverse alphabetical order, as a numbered list.

1. tabla
2. drum
3. cymbal
Finish a thank-you email for me. One or two sentences, and the very last words must be "Best wishes."
Thank you again for your help with the report. Best wishes.
Four household chores, please: one per line, exactly two words each.

Wash dishes
Sweep floors
Water plants
Fold clothes
One sentence about feeling proud, please, with exactly one comma in it.
When I finished the race, I felt proud of myself.
Suggest three rainy-day hobbies in a numbered list, with every idea starting with the letter B.

1. Baking biscuits
2. Building paper boats
3. Beading a bracelet
What is a leap year? One sentence, under 20 words, using the word "extra".
A leap year has an extra day, February 29, added to keep the calendar correct.
Write a question about a school library in all lowercase, ending with a question mark.
do you know which shelf holds the poetry books?
Name four parts of a flower, comma-separated, in alphabetical order.
anther, petal, sepal, stigma
Write a two-line riddle about a snail, without using the word "slow".

I carry my house wherever I roam,
and I leave a silver trail on the way home.
A Holi poster needs a title of four words, all in capital letters.
COLOURS, JOY, AND FRIENDS
Give exactly three kinds of dal as a numbered list, all in lowercase.

1. toor dal
2. moong dal
3. masoor dal
Help me ask a hotel receptionist for an extra pillow. One sentence in question form that uses "could".
Could you please send an extra pillow to my room?
Describe a cycle rickshaw ride in two sentences that both begin with "The".
The rickshaw rattles gently along the narrow lane. The driver rings his bell at every turn.
Give a one-line cloudy-day forecast under 12 words that includes the word "chance".
Expect grey skies all day, with a chance of drizzle.
What makes a good listener? Three dash bullets, each under seven words.

- Look at the speaker
- Wait before you reply
- Ask a kind question
I have a job interview. Give me two lines, labelled "Greeting:" and "Intro:", that I can say at the start.

Greeting: Good morning, it is nice to meet you.
Intro: I am Sana, and I have just finished a diploma in design.
Four things in a city park, please. Lowercase, one per line, nothing more.

bench
fountain
swing
pond
A school choir needs a motto of exactly six words.
Many voices joined in one song.
Describe a peacock in one sentence of exactly 12 words.
The peacock spreads its shimmering blue and green tail like a fan.
Please write a haiku about a drum.

The drum begins soft
Then the whole street starts to dance
Even the dogs sway
Two sentences on kite flying: the first with exactly five words, the second with exactly seven.
Bright kites fill the sky. Children run across the field with strings.
How do you make a bed? Exactly four numbered steps of fewer than seven words each.

1. Pull off the old sheet.
2. Spread the clean sheet.
3. Tuck in the corners.
4. Fluff up the pillow.
Which three items make up a simple school uniform? Lowercase, separated by commas.
shirt, trousers, shoes
My friend looks sad. What can I ask to start a talk? Question form only, under 12 words.
Would you like to tell me what is on your mind?
Describe ice melting in exactly three sentences, each with no more than five words.
Ice gets warm. It turns soft. Then it becomes water.
Give me two numbered steps for shutting down a computer, each under ten words.

1. Save your work and close all files.
2. Choose Shut Down from the menu.
Say what a wallet is in one sentence, using the words "cards" and "notes".
A wallet is a small case for carrying cards and notes.
Name four insects in alphabetical order, lowercase, one per line.

ant
bee
beetle
butterfly
Describe Christmas morning in two sentences, ending the second with an exclamation mark.
The family wakes early and gathers around the tree. What a joyful morning!
Give three Indian cities as a numbered list, each followed by its state in brackets.

1. Jaipur (Rajasthan)
2. Kochi (Kerala)
3. Pune (Maharashtra)
Message my aunt about her trip, in question form only, with exactly two questions.
How was your trip, Aunty? Did you enjoy the mountains?
Write one sentence that uses both "between" and "among".
I sat between two friends, and we walked among the trees.
Pick four school subjects and list them one per line in alphabetical order.

art
history
maths
science
Make a poster line about covering your mouth when you cough. All capital letters, fewer than eight words.
COVER YOUR MOUTH WHEN YOU COUGH
Can you write a haiku about a banyan tree?

The banyan stands wide
Roots hang down like quiet ropes
Birds sing in its shade
Spell out READ as an acrostic about reading, with one line for each letter.

Reading opens new doors.
Every page is a surprise.
Adventures wait inside.
Dreams begin here.
Describe the aroma of fresh bread in one sentence without the words "smell" or "warm".
Fresh bread fills the kitchen with a soft, golden aroma.
Write three questions a visitor could ask a guide at an old fort. Number them, and keep each under nine words.

1. How old is this fort?
2. Who lived here long ago?
3. Which gate was the main entrance?
Capture nervousness in a single lowercase sentence, shorter than 15 words.
my hands shake a little before the curtain rises.
Four sports played in water, please, one per line, lowercase, in alphabetical order.

diving
rowing
surfing
swimming
Write a sentence about a dusty summer afternoon. It must begin with "When" and have fewer than 18 words.
When the afternoon turns dusty, the whole street goes quiet under the heavy sun.
Leave three notes for my flatmate, one per line, starting with "Please", "Thanks" and "See you" in that order.

Please lock the door when you leave.
Thanks for cooking last night.
See you at dinner.
Suggest three party games as a numbered list. Every game name must be exactly two words.

1. Musical chairs
2. Treasure hunt
3. Pass parcel
Write a sentence of exactly ten words about a street vendor that includes "cart" and "evening".
The vendor pushes his cart through the street each evening.
What sounds do a cow, a dog and a duck make? Answer in that order, lowercase, comma-separated.
moo, bark, quack
I want to ask my manager for next Friday off. Exactly three sentences, and do not use the word "need".
Dear Sir, may I take next Friday off for a family function? I will finish all my tasks before I go. Thank you for considering my request.
Give me the first line of a song about a train. Exactly eight words.
The train sings softly through the sleeping hills.
Three words that describe a villain in a story, please, comma-separated and in alphabetical order.
cruel, cunning, selfish
Give the opposite of brave, rough and tidy, in that order, as a numbered list.

1. cowardly
2. smooth
3. messy
How do plants take in water? Two numbered steps, each under twelve words.

1. Roots take in water from the soil.
2. The water travels up the stem to the leaves.
Write a Navratri invitation in exactly two sentences that uses the words "dance" and "lights".
Come and dance with us tonight in the colourful garba circle. The lights will glow until late.
Describe my grandfather's old chair in one sentence that ends with the word "story".
Grandfather's old wooden chair creaks every time he begins a story.
What are two tips for travelling on a crowded bus? Number them. The first tip begins with "Hold" and the second with "Keep".

1. Hold the rail firmly.
2. Keep your bag in front.
Describe baking a cake in five lines that start with Mix, Pour, Bake, Cool and Serve, in that order.

Mix flour, sugar and eggs
Pour the batter into a tin
Bake it until golden
Cool it on a rack
Serve a slice with tea
What does a morning alarm do? Under 12 words, please.
It rings at a set time to wake you up.
Explain a battery to a child in exactly two sentences, and use the word "power".
A battery stores energy inside a small case. It gives power to things like torches and toys.
A flooded road: write one sentence about it that has "because" in the middle, not at the start or end, in under 15 words.
I stayed inside because the road was flooded.
Sunrise poem, four lines, where every line has exactly three words.

Pale gold light
Spills over hills
Birds begin singing
A new day
Name three feelings that all start with the letter J, comma-separated, nothing else.
joy, jealousy, jitters
Write a three-line pep talk for a football team. Each line must be under seven words, and the last line must be a command.

We have trained for this day.
Trust the player beside you.
Go out and play!
Give four fruits for a salad as a numbered list, in lowercase and alphabetical order.

1. apple
2. banana
3. grapes
4. papaya
Announce a shop sale in one sentence that includes the number 50 in digits and the word "today".
Everything on the shelf is 50 percent off today.
Tell me how to get from the bus stop to the library, using exactly three numbered steps of fewer than ten words each.

1. Walk straight along the main road.
2. Turn left at the bakery.
3. The library is on your right.
Write to a friend who has moved away: three sentences, with the last one a question.
I miss you already. The classroom feels quiet without your jokes. When can we talk on a video call?
Tell me a fact about bees in one sentence under 15 words that includes "flowers".
Bees visit flowers to collect nectar and carry pollen as they go.
Set a general-knowledge quiz question about oceans. Question form only, ten words or fewer.
Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
List four healthy habits, numbered, with one word for each.

1. Sleeping
2. Walking
3. Stretching
4. Washing
A rhyming two-line poem about frost, please.

Frost paints the window glass at night,
And morning turns it silver-bright.
Write a railway announcement in exactly two sentences that uses the word "platform".
The express to Chennai will arrive shortly at platform four. Please stand behind the yellow line.
Make a sentence that correctly uses "their", "there" and "they're".
They're waiting there with their bags.
What should I do after school? Three lines that start with "First,", "Then," and "Finally,".

First, wash your hands.
Then, eat a snack.
Finally, start your homework.
Suggest two team lunch ideas as bullet points that start with "#", each under six words.

# Pizza on the terrace
# Picnic in the park
What is a raga? One sentence, and do not use the word "music".
A raga is a melodic framework of notes that musicians use to create a mood.
An Onam wish under 12 words, with the word "flowers", please.
Happy Onam! May your doorstep bloom with flowers and joy.
Name four kinds of natural water, one per line, in alphabetical order.

lake
pond
river
stream
Two sentences on the Moon, please. The first must start with "The" and the second with "It".
The Moon travels around the Earth. It shines because it reflects sunlight.
Summarise a story about a lost dog finding its way home in exactly six words.
Lost dog wanders, finds home again.
A Mother's Day line, please, under ten words, ending with the word "you".
Thank you for everything, Amma. I love you.
Give one exam-day tip as a command, in a single sentence of fewer than ten words.
Read every question carefully before you begin writing.
Write two lines about watering plants at dawn. Each line must have exactly six words.

I water the roses at dawn.
The leaves shine with tiny drops.
One sentence about a winter evening, please, in which no word has more than four letters.
It is dark by six and the air is cold.
About a cyclist: a sentence that begins with "Slowly" and ends with "hill".
Slowly the cyclist pushed her way up the steep hill.
Name three desert animals as a numbered list, in lowercase, each followed by a colon and one describing word.

1. camel: tall
2. lizard: quick
3. scorpion: tiny
Write a thank-you note for a book in exactly 14 words.
Thank you for the very lovely book. I will gladly read it this weekend.
Write a haiku about the school bell.

The bell rings at last
Bags swing and children rush out
Silence fills the hall
I would like a haiku about hot tea on a cold morning.

Steam curls from the cup
My cold fingers hold it close
Morning feels softer
Give me a haiku about a night train.

The night train rushes
Windows glow like moving stars
Far towns fall asleep
Compose a haiku about summer holidays at a grandparent's house.

Mango days stretch long
Cousins laugh beneath the fan
Summer will not end
Give four tips for a first-time cyclist as a numbered list. Each tip should be under six words.

1. Wear a helmet.
2. Check your brakes.
3. Ride slowly at first.
4. Stay on quiet roads.
Name three Indian sweets, numbered, one word each.

1. Jalebi
2. Laddu
3. Barfi
I have a pen pal in another town. Give me two questions to ask her about it, in question form only.
What is the weather like in your town today? Which festival do people enjoy most there?
Help me ask my teacher about homework after class. One question only, under 12 words.
Could you explain question three again, please?
Suggest three questions for a family dinner talk. Only questions, one per line, no numbers.

What was the best part of your day?
What made you laugh today?
What are you looking forward to this week?
Tell me about a kitten playing, in one sentence, and avoid the word "cute".
The kitten tumbled after a ball of wool and tangled itself in the string.
Show me three ways to say thank you without using the word "thank" or "thanks". One per line.

I really appreciate your help.
You have been very kind.
That was a big help to me.
About a bus ride on a stormy day, write one sentence, avoiding any word that contains "rain".
The window blurred with drops while the bus crawled through the grey traffic.
What can a lonely new student do to meet people? One sentence, without the word "friend" or "friends".
Smile at someone who sits near you and ask about their favourite game.
Include the words "bee" and "jasmine" in a sentence about a garden.
A small bee hummed around the jasmine by the gate.
Use the word "unless" in a sentence about a picnic.
We will have the picnic on Sunday unless the sky turns dark.
Two sentences about a bakery, please. The first must include "morning" and the second "crumbs".
The bakery opens early every morning. Customers leave with warm bags and a few crumbs on their sleeves.
Give me exactly six words about a bicycle bell, as one sentence.
The bell rings, and birds scatter.
Describe a rooftop at night in exactly 11 words.
Stars freckle the sky while distant trains murmur below the rooftop.
What is a library for? Answer in fewer than ten words.
A library lends books and offers a quiet place.
Text my mother that I reached school safely. Keep it under ten words.
Reached school safely, Mummy. Will call at lunch.
What is an echo? One sentence, and use the word "bounces".
An echo is a voice that bounces back from a wall or a hill.
Tell a ten-year-old why we have seasons, in one sentence that includes the word "tilts".
We have seasons because the Earth tilts as it travels around the Sun.
Describe a train journey in exactly four sentences.
The train leaves at dawn. Fields roll past the window. A vendor sells hot tea. We arrive just before noon.
Write three lines about a bus stop, each starting with "At".

At dawn, the bench is empty.
At noon, students crowd around it.
At night, one lamp keeps watch.
Share three facts about owls. Each should be its own line beginning with "Owls".

Owls hunt mostly at night.
Owls can turn their heads far around.
Owls swallow small prey whole.
Four lines about falling leaves, please, each starting with the letter L.

Leaves turn gold and red,
Light falls softly on the lane,
Long shadows stretch out,
Loud winds carry them away.
Make an acrostic of the word HOME, with a short phrase on each line.

Hot rice on the table
Open windows and fresh air
My mother's laughter
Evenings together
Write an acrostic of RAIN, one line for each letter.

Rooftops drum softly
All the puddles ripple
In the lane, children splash
Nothing smells like wet earth
Write a good-night message for a friend in two sentences, all lowercase.
good night, and sleep well. see you at school tomorrow.
Name the three main meals of the day on one line, comma-separated, in lowercase.
breakfast, lunch, dinner
Make a sign for a library door that asks for quiet. Capital letters only, fewer than eight words.
PLEASE KEEP QUIET INSIDE THE LIBRARY
Write a one-line shout for supporters at a kabaddi match, in all capitals.
COME ON, TEAM, SHOW THEM YOUR STRENGTH!
Sort these colours alphabetically as a numbered list: violet, green, orange, blue, red.

1. blue
2. green
3. orange
4. red
5. violet
Put these animals in alphabetical order on one line, separated by commas: yak, goat, lion, camel, horse.
camel, goat, horse, lion, yak
List three Indian languages, one per line, in lowercase and in reverse alphabetical order.

tamil
marathi
hindi
How do I wash a school shirt by hand? Five numbered steps, each under ten words.

1. Soak the shirt in clean water.
2. Rub soap on the dirty parts.
3. Scrub gently with your hands.
4. Rinse until the water runs clear.
5. Hang it in the sun to dry.
Explain how to post a letter in three numbered steps of under eight words each.

1. Write the address on the envelope.
2. Stick a stamp in the corner.
3. Drop it in a post box.
Give two reasons to visit a museum as bullet points that start with "*". Each must be under eight words.

* To learn about the past
* To see rare objects
Name three indoor plants as bullet points starting with "+", all in lowercase.

+ money plant
+ aloe vera
+ snake plant
Give exactly four adjectives for a sunny day, comma-separated, all lowercase.
warm, bright, clear, cheerful
Name exactly five Indian states that start with the letter M, one per line, in alphabetical order.

Madhya Pradesh
Maharashtra
Manipur
Meghalaya
Mizoram
Write a short note to a friend about our day out. It must end with the words "See you soon."
I enjoyed the day with you so much. See you soon.
Write a two-line card for a retiring teacher. Line one under eight words; line two must include "grateful".

Thank you for every lesson.
We are grateful for your kindness and patience.
Describe a mango tree in two sentences, and keep every sentence to eight words or fewer.
The mango tree shades our whole yard. Its fruit ripens every summer.
Suggest two names for a school magazine, one per line, each exactly two words in title case.

Bright Pages
School Voices
Say something about the sun in one sentence, using no word that contains the letter "e".
Today a big, bright sun is shining on a town.
Tell a tiny story of three sentences about a boy who loses his shoe at a village fair. Use the word "gate".
Arun lost his shoe while running at the village fair. He searched every stall and found it near the gate. Who had carried it there?
In the past tense, tell me about a school trip. One sentence of exactly nine words.
We visited the science museum and loved every room.
Describe your favourite season in two sentences. Use the word "because" exactly once.
My favourite season is the monsoon because the air smells fresh. Everyone slows down to listen to the rain.
Give me the opening line of a bedtime story in exactly ten words, and include the word "dragon".
Once a gentle dragon lived behind the old school wall.
List three things you need to cook rice, one per line, with no bullets or numbers.

Pot
Water
